conventions.convention: Polynomial approximation uses real continuous targets on I=[a,b] with a<b, degrees n≥0, and the uniform norm; the polynomial comparison class includes zero.

Rational candidates have coprime real numerator and denominator with degree bounds (m,n), denominator strictly positive throughout I, and denominator coefficient Euclidean norm one. The weight is continuous and strictly positive throughout I.
For nonzero reduced r=p/q, d=min(m−deg p,n−deg q) and N=m+n−d. For zero, the pair is (0,1), d=n, and N=m. The candidate's alternation count is N+2.
Polynomial reference nodes increase strictly, and the signed Remez level is fixed by p(x_i)+(-1)^i λ=f(x_i). A certificate compares the global norm with |λ|.

Both budgeted algorithms iterate over k=0,…,B, permitting B+1 solves and at most B+1 oracle calls. Termination is conditional on terminating input procedures; neither algorithm claims iterative convergence.
The rational exchange procedure returns immediately on a defective solver candidate instead of applying the normal m+n+2-point count.

load_bearing.statement: For nonzero r=p/q in the admissible family with defect d and N=m+n−d, {uq−pv : u∈P_m, v∈P_n}=P_N. For r=0 with p=0,q=1,d=n,N=m, the same equality holds.

For a nondegenerate compact interval, nonnegative degrees, a continuous real target, and a strictly positive continuous weight, a best admissible rational approximant exists and is unique. A candidate with positive weighted error is best if and only if its weighted residual has N+2 ordered alternating global extrema, where N=m+n−d for that candidate.

If a continuous real residual on [a,b], a<b, has positive uniform norm and no n+2 increasing active-extrema points with alternating signs, there is a real polynomial h of degree at most n such that e(x)h(x)>0 at every active extremum.
A nonzero real polynomial of degree at most n cannot have nonzero alternating values at n+2 strictly increasing real nodes.
For N+2 increasing real nodes and w_i=∏_{j≠i}(x_i−x_j), every g∈P_N satisfies Σ_i g(x_i)/w_i=0. If ε(-1)^i g(x_i)≥0 for one fixed ε∈{−1,1}, then g is the zero polynomial.
For I=[a,b] with a<b, m,n≥0, continuous real f, and strictly positive continuous w, an admissible rational function attains E_{m,n}(f,w;I).

A polynomial of degree at most n equals its cardinal interpolation sum at any n+1 distinct real nodes; consequently every coefficient is bounded by a fixed constant times the maximum absolute sampled value.
A best degree-at-most-n uniform polynomial approximant with positive error on a nondegenerate compact interval has n+2 ordered alternating global residual extrema.
At any n+2 distinct increasing nodes in I, for any real-valued data f, there is a unique (p,λ)∈P_n(I)×R satisfying p(x_i)+(-1)^i λ=f(x_i).
For a continuous real target on [a,b], a<b, a degree-at-most-n candidate with positive global uniform error E is best if its residual equals σ(-1)^i E at n+2 ordered nodes.

published_dependencies.used_for: Agreement of the local best-error definition with the published convention on [-1,1].
Continuity on the interval, including endpoints and cancelled denominator zeros.
Formal coefficient representations and degree conventions.
Continuity of the distance function in the sign-block construction.
Repeated factorization and cancellation at zeros of a limiting denominator.
Continuity of polynomial residuals, products, absolute values, and quotients on their nonvanishing-denominator domains.
Reduced rational representations and the kernel calculation for the rational perturbation map.
Compactness of closed bounded coefficient sets and attainment of continuous extrema on nonempty compact sets.
Roots between opposite polynomial signs and constant sign of nowhere-zero reduced denominators.
Interpolation identities, zero-count contradictions, finite denominator zero sets, and uniqueness.
Product degree bounds in the perturbation-space and cancellation arguments.
Bijectivity of the polynomial Remez system and dimension of the rational perturbation image.

concerns.concern: Step 2.2 says, “By step 1.2, r has N+2 alternating nodes,” but step 1.2 only sets up the contradiction and constructs a perturbation; necessity is completed in step 2.1. Likewise step 3.1 attributes the two directions to steps 1.1 and 1.2 while omitting step 2.1. The complete argument is present, but these conclusion references point to the setup rather than its discharge.

seams_checked.note: The consuming page explicitly describes minimax as contextual, disclaims a minimax guarantee for finite-sample AAA, and uses no assigned minimax item as an item-level proof premise. The supplier page makes no AAA assertion or reverse logical use. Its polynomial and defect-sensitive rational guarantees are not overstated across this seam.
